title: TokenWeave: Efficient Compute-Communication Overlap for Distributed LLM Inference
technique: token-splitting compute-communication overlap with fused AllReduce-RMSNorm kernel using NVLS/Multimem on few SMs

optimized_metrics.evidence: Even with high-speed interconnects like NVLink, communication overheads remain a major performance bottleneck. For example, Figure 1 shows that communication accounts for 9-23% of the end-to-end inference latency

headline_claim.text: up to 1.28x speedup in latency (baseline/ours) and up to 1.19x higher throughput (ours/baseline) across multiple models and workloads

reported_metrics.where: §5.2.1: bounded by chunked prefills (evaluation setup only; re-pass)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For end-to-end (e2e) results, we also perform warm-up and then measure latency using time.perf_counter(). We disable prefix caching and ignore detokenization time
metric_definitions.notes: 'Latency' = wall-clock time of a forward pass / batch (prefill-only batches of fixed token count), not request latency.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Metrics: Latency and Tokens per second
metric_definitions.notes: Tokens per second; input vs output counting not defined.

slo_spec: mentions interactive SLOs qualitatively; none specified
load_regime: fixed (input,output)-length traces and ShareGPT/arXiv traces run offline with chunked prefill (chunk 2K, 4K for Mixtral); single-iteration microbenchmarks
tradeoff_acknowledged: Chunk size trades TBT against throughput (smaller chunks -> lower TBT, lower throughput); TokenWeave applied only to batches with 1K+ tokens.
extractor_notes: No TTFT/TPOT/percentile reported; 'latency' is forward-pass latency. TBT is invoked only to justify chunked-prefill config.
